content.text: {"evidenceSpans":[{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0001","evidenceText":"OWP FIM is linked with the NWM for operational purposes, utilizing streamflow inputs, to produce FIM at a continental scale.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0002","evidenceText":"We evaluated various validation data sources for operational use, each with its own strengths and weaknesses, including high water marks (HWMs) (Breaker et al., [2016](#page-27-27); Musser et al., [2017;](#page-29-32) Watson et al., [2017\\)](#page-30-30), remote sensing observations (Aristizabal et al., [2020;](#page-27-9) Aristizabal & Judge, [2021\\)](#page-27-10), and modeled extents from hyper-resolution, local models (McEnery et al., [2005](#page-29-4)).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0003","evidenceText":"Although they have advantages, the three data sources mentioned do not have streamflow information, which is required by OWP FIM.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0004","evidenceText":"Using the NWM as a source of streamflow input would be a logical choice due to its operational use, but this would introduce hydro-climatic uncertainties that could impact the results of adding a multi-fluvial source extension to HAND.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0005","evidenceText":"On the other hand, relying on point sources of streamflow or stage, such as gages, would eliminate this limitation, but limit the information available to only a single source of inundation at a specific site.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0006","evidenceText":"Given these limitations, we investigated the use of existing HEC-RAS based models to address the limitations caused by hydro-climatic uncertainties and sparse streamflow inputs.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0007","evidenceText":"Our HAND based approach coupled with SRCs requires streamflow as input and is agnostic as to the source of that streamflow whether forecasted, observed, or probablistic.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0008","evidenceText":"Due to this fact, evaluation of our relative elevation CFIM method was conducted by comparison to the HEC-RAS 1D models produced within FEMA region 6 (Base Level Engineering (BLE) Tools and Resources, [2021](#page-27-21); estBFE Viewer, [2021;](#page-30-22) USACE, [2022\\)](#page-30-23).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0009","evidenceText":"This data set was selected due to its large spatial coverage, availability of cross-sections with streamflow information, higher level of sophistication when compared to HAND, engineering scale detail, and a storied use in the literature as an evaluation data set (Afshari et al., [2018](#page-27-11); Bates et al., [2016;](#page-27-28) Cook & Merwade, [2009;](#page-27-29) Criss & Nelson, [2022;](#page-27-30) Follum et al., [2017](#page-28-30); Hu & Demir, [2021](#page-28-31); Li & Demir, [2022](#page-28-32); Li et al., [2022;](#page-28-33) Rajib et al., [2016;](#page-29-33) Wing et al., [2017;](#page-30-31) Wing et al., [2017](#page-30-31); Zheng, Maidment, et al., [2018](#page-30-12); Zheng, Maidment, et al., [2018](#page-30-12)).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0010","evidenceText":"We selected 49 available HUC8s, shown in Figure [7](#page-16-0), which span about 185 thousand km2 across nine states.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0011","evidenceText":"The maps of the 1% recurrence flow (1 in 100 years) and the 0.2% recurrence flow (1 in 500 years) are furnished by InFRM as well as the corresponding discharges and mapping extents for evaluation.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0012","evidenceText":"We did exclude NWM V2.1 Reservoirs from evaluation because these are not properly accounted for in the inundation sourced from OWP FIM.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0013","evidenceText":"Since the BLE does account for reservoir inundation, some of the BLE reservoir inundation extents extend beyond the NWM reservoir geometries contributing to false negatives (FNs), or under-prediction.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0014","evidenceText":"By using the same HEC-RAS derived discharges and FIM extents for creating maps with OWP FIM, we are able to separate out errors introduced by NWM inputs and processes including land surface interactions, groundwater fluxes, atmospheric forcings, hydraulic routing, and others that would have potentially affected our conclusions if we had used NWM forecasted discharges.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0015","evidenceText":"We elected to spatially intersect the HEC-RAS cross sections with the NWM stream network assigning the 1% and 0.2% flow rates to each NWM reach.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0016","evidenceText":"To handle multiple intersections, we opted to use a filter to select the median discharge value attributed to each NWM reach.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0017","evidenceText":"Additionally, the stream network of the InFRM furnished models are of higher stream densities and bifurcation ratios, as evident in Figure [8](#page-16-1), leading to a significant amount of FNs along headwater streams with unit Horton-Strahler order due to the lack of representation of these additional headwater streams in the NWM network.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0018","evidenceText":"While the limitations are noted, this method does best to detangle the influence of exogenous variables that we do not wish to study in this comparison.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0019","evidenceText":"The metrics employed in this study to evaluate inundation extents include CSI, Probability of Detection (POD), and False Alarm Ratio (FAR) and are presented in Equations [6](#page-17-0)[–8,](#page-17-1) respectively.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0020","evidenceText":"To calculate these secondary metrics, one must define three primary metrics starting with true positives (TP) which is predicted wet and wet in the BLE benchmark data set.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0021","evidenceText":"The two types of errors consist of false positives (FP), or type I errors, which is dry in the benchmark but predicted wet and false negatives (FN), or type II errors, which is wet in the benchmark but predicted dry.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0022","evidenceText":"Lastly, the reader may come across true negatives (TN) which is defined as dry in both","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0023","evidenceText":"the benchmark and predicted datasets.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0024","evidenceText":"Maximizing POD indicates a model's ability to detect the given threat of interest, inundation, while minimizing FAR is sought to indicate a models ability in reducing FN errors.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0025","evidenceText":"In other words, POD is an indicator of model skill in inundated regions while FAR is an indicator of model skill in non-inundated regions.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0026","evidenceText":"Some work by Gerapetritis and Pelissier ([2004\\)](#page-28-34) denotes CSI a good proxy for measuring a forecasting system's utility in protecting life and property and has been shown as mathematically optimized when POD = 1 − FAR.","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0027","evidenceText":"While these metrics are commonly employed in the evaluation of FIM and binary weather prediction communities in general, they do come with some notable limitations including frequency dependence in the case of CSI and FAR (Gerapetritis & Pelissier, [2004](#page-28-34); Jolliffe & Stephenson, [2012](#page-28-35); Schaefer, [1990;](#page-29-34) Stephens et al., [2014](#page-30-32)).","locatorAnchor":null},{"evidenceSpanID":"evidence-0028","evidenceText":"Lastly, approximately six HUC8s do not have NWM MS reaches thus we imputed the metrics for FR for these sites as the best available forecasting capability to compare GMS metrics
